\emph{You must show work to receive credit. Do not use a calculator/computer
for problems with a }$\bigstar$\emph{. Each problem is of equal value. }

\textbf{Use the given conditions to write an equation for the line
in slope-intercept form, if possible.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item Slope$=-3$, passing through $(6,6)$.\vfill
\item Slope $=4$ passing through $(7,3)$.\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Find the equation of the least squares line. }
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item \label{enu:The-total-amount}The paired data below consists of the
test scores of $6$ randomly selected students and the number of hours
they studied for the test.

\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item []%
\begin{tabular}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c}
Hours $(x)$ & 5 & 10 & 4 & 6 & 10 & 9\tabularnewline
\hline 
Score $(y)$ & 64 & 86 & 69 & 86 & 59 & 87\tabularnewline
\end{tabular}\xspace\xspace
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Write a cost function for the problem. Assume that the relationship
is linear.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item A moving firm charges a flat fee of \$40 plus \$35 per hour. Let $C(x)$
be the cost in dollars of using the moving firm for $x$ hours.\xspace
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Solve the system of two equations in two unknowns.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item $\bigstar$ $\begin{array}{r}
x+y=-2\\
x-y=18
\end{array}$\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Solve the system of two equations in two unknowns.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item $\bigstar$ $\begin{array}{r}
x+6y=-5\\
-4x+7y=20
\end{array}$\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\newpage

\textbf{Solve the problem.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item A digital pen manufacturer has decided to come out with a new and
affordable pen. The fixed cost for the production of this new pen
line is \$16,600 and the variable costs are \$68 per pen. The company
expects to sell the pens for \$159 a piece. Formulate a function $C(x)$
for the total cost of producing $x$ new pens and a function $R(x)$
for the total revenue generated by the sales of $x$ pens. \vfill
\item There are 600 people at a concert. The admission prices was \$10 for
adults and \$5 for children. The admission receipts were \$4650. How
many adults and how many children attended? \vfill
\item Sweet Honey Bakery serves desserts. Two servings of yogurt and three
servings of apple cobbler has 1670 calories. One serving of yogurt
and two servings of apple cobbler has 1030 calories. Find the caloric
content of each item.\vfill
\item After two years on the job, a therapists salary was \$60,000. After
seven years on the job, her salary was \$72,500. Let $y$ represent
her salary after $x$ years on the job. Assuming that a change in
her salary over time can be approximated by a straight line, give
an equation for this line in the form $y=mx+b$.\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\newpage
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item FedUps delivers packages which cost \$3.00 per package to deliver.
The fixed cost to run the delivery truck is \$250 per day. If the
company charges \$6.00 per package, how many packages must be delivered
to make a profit of \$131?\vfill
\item A shoe company will make a new design of walking shoe. The fixed cost
for the production will be \$24,000. The variable cost will be \$31
per pair of shoes. The shoes will sell for \$106 for each pair. How
many pairs of shoes will have to be sold for the company to break
even on this new line of shoes?\vfill
\item Let the supply and demand functions for for gourmet hot chocolate
packs be given by 
\[
p=S(q)=\frac{9}{4}q\mbox{ and }p=D(q)=70-\frac{5}{4}q
\]
where $p$ is the price in dollars and $q$ is the number of batches.
Find the equilibrium quantity and the equilibrium price.\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Find the slope of the line passing through the given pair
of points .}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item $(3,4)$ and $(3,-8)$\xspace
\item $(-4,1)$ and $(-9,1)$\xspace
\item $(5,-5)$ and $(-7,-3)$\xspace
\item $(6,5)$ and $(-4,5)$\xspace
\end{enumerate}
\newpage

\textbf{The sizes of two matrices $A$ and $B$ are given. Find the
sizes of the product $AB$ and the product $BA$, whenever these products
exist.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item $A$ is $1\times3$, and $B$ is $3\times1$.

\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item $AB$:\vspace{.5cm}
\item $BA$:\vspace{.5cm}
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Find the matrix if possible.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item $\bigstar$ $\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rrr}
1 & 2 & 3\\
4 & 5 & 0
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rr}
3 & 0\\
-2 & 1\\
0 & 3
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$\vfill
\item $\bigstar$ $\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rrr}
1 & 2 & 3\\
4 & 5 & 0
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rr}
3 & 0\\
-2 & 1
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Solve the problem.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item $\bigstar$ Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rr}
-1 & 0\\
6 & 3
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$ Find $-2A$. \vfill
\item $\bigstar$ Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rr}
-1 & 0\\
6 & 3
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rr}
-1 & 6\\
3 & 1
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$. Find $A-B$. \vfill
\item $\bigstar$ Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rr}
-1 & 0\\
6 & 3
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rr}
-1 & 6\\
3 & 1
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$. Find $A+B$. \vfill
\item $\bigstar$ Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rr}
-1 & 0\\
6 & 3
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rr}
-1 & 6\\
3 & 1
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$. Find $2A+B$. \vfill
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{SHORT ANSWER. Write the word or phrase that best completes
each statement or answers the question.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item In one or more paragraphs, explain what it means to ``break even''
in business.
\end{enumerate}
